findings.text: non-blocking: the inline row filter repeats ledger._active_records (reckon/ledger.py:2019) in predicate and shape, so the index's activity rule now has two copies and a change to one silently admits a different row population under a derivation than outside it.

non-blocking: the fragment records that with the fixture corrected the file still failed, measuring one derivation built the index 2 times, but no log of that arm exists among the run's logs or in its manifest test_logs, so the product cause rests on a measurement no log records.

non-blocking: derivation_run_rows resolves the held pass by project alone (reckon/crew/obligations.py:3729), so where _ledger_read_root keeps the checkout's own root (reckon/crew/obligations.py:3375) the utilisation reader is answered from rows read against a different ledger file than its own bounded read names, and tests/test_a_derivation_builds_the_ledger_index_once.py:204 compares only held_worktrees across the two routes.

non-blocking: the gate log names the tree and the command but no scheduler or partition, and both declared arms ran under a bare pytest with SLURM_JOB_ID unrecorded, so the done_when's requirement that the arms be all_debug jobs is not visible from the records the run kept.
